The Image of God in a Kingdom

Good evening. Over the past two weeks I have been spending time studying the Kingdom of God and what it means for a kingdom to be a kingdom. I will be sharing a series of blogs that address this subject. Section 1 is all about the image of God in a kingdom.

A well known section in the gospel of Matthew that most of us have read or heard many times reveals a very important fact.

Matthew 22:15–22

Then the Pharisees went out and laid plans to trap him in his words. They sent their disciples to him along with the Herodians. “Teacher,” they said, “we know that you are a man of integrity and that you teach the way of God in accordance with the truth. You aren’t swayed by others, because you pay no attention to who they are. Tell us then, what is your opinion? Is it right to pay the imperial tax to Caesar or not?”

But Jesus, knowing their evil intent, said, “You hypocrites, why are you trying to trap me? Show me the coin used for paying the tax.” They brought him a denarius, and he asked them, “Whose image is this? And whose inscription?”

“Caesar’s,” they replied.

Then he said to them, “So give back to Caesar what is Caesar’s, and to God what is God’s.”

The Pharisees came to trap Jesus with a question about taxes. Should they pay Caesar or not? If he said yes, he would have looked like a Roman collaborator. If he said no, he would have been arrested. This was a delicate situation.

Jesus asked for a coin. Someone handed him a denarius, a small silver Roman coin that served as the standard currency of the day. He held it up and asked them one question: whose image was on it?

Caesar’s, they said.

Then give to Caesar what is Caesar’s, he told them. And give to God what is God’s.

Most of us have spent our whole lives hearing the first half of that sentence and missing the second half. For me it had always been a statement about taxes, and I moved on without ever reflecting on what Jesus actually said next.

Give to God what is God’s.

That coin represented something. In the ancient world, the image on a coin was not a design preference as we see on money today, or a cultural tradition. It was a legal declaration of ownership. Every coin in the Roman Empire carried the emperor’s face because every coin was his. The image represented a voice that declared in whose world you were living, under whose authority you were governed, and whose name backed the currency in your hand. To use the coin was to acknowledge, whether you thought about it or not, that you were living inside someone else’s kingdom.

So when Jesus held up that denarius and asked whose image was on it, there was a deeper truth he wanted to reveal.

He was setting up the most important question anyone would ever be asked.

Because if the coin bearing Caesar’s image belonged to Caesar, then what bore God’s image belonged to God.

And that left one question hanging in the air that Jesus did not need to say out loud, because every person in that crowd already heard it the moment he spoke.

What bears God’s image?

The answer was there from the very first page of the very first book, Genesis was written before the law, before the covenant, before Israel, before everything else. So God created mankind in his own image. In the image of God he created them.

We do. Every human being carries the image of God pressed into the core of who they are as the most foundational fact of human existence. We are the living currency of the Kingdom of God.

An Identity That Cannot Be Revoked

We live in a world that tells us identity is something we construct for ourselves. We choose who we are, we define what we stand for, and we build our sense of self from our achievements, our relationships, our choices, and the story we tell about our own lives. And when those things shift, when the job disappears, when the relationship ends, or when the version of ourselves we worked so hard to build starts to crack under pressure, we discover that a self constructed identity has no foundation underneath it.

But the image of God was not something you constructed. It was placed in you before you made a single decision about anything. Before you succeeded at anything or failed at anything. Before anyone told you who you were or who you were not. Before your best moment and before your worst.

The image was already there, and it does not depend on your performance to remain in place. Your identity is not primarily something you built; it is something you received when you were born into this earth. And it cannot be revoked by failure, by other people’s opinions, by your own darkest seasons, or by anything the world does to you.

The Person Sitting Across From You

There is one more thing the coin tells us, and it is perhaps the most demanding of all.

Every person you encounter every day carries the same image. The colleague who makes your Monday harder than it needs to be, the family member who knows exactly which wound to press, the person whose choices you fundamentally disagree with, the one you have quietly decided is not worth your full attention. Every single one of them has the King’s face stamped into who they are. And the way we treat them is the way we treat the one whose image they carry.

There is no such thing as an insignificant person. There is no interaction that falls below the level of the image of God. There is no one we are permitted to write off.

The Pharisees came to trap Jesus with a coin and walked away carrying a question they could not ignore.

Never forget who you belong to. And whose image you bear.

God bless you.

Good evening! Over the weekend our church was "confronted" with a powerful word that really spoke to my heart. The message shared is, and should be, at the centre of our walk with God, but it is also a message of truth to non-believers, a message that "cuts deep" to the core of us all. We have to know and understand the John 15 message that Jesus shared, to ultimately draw close to Go
So what was the message?
At its core, we are compared to branches grafted and connected to a vine, Jesus, in a vineyard. "I am the vine; you are the branches. If you remain in me and I in you, you will bear much fruit; apart from me you can do nothing" (John 15:5, NIV). It speaks of our lives being pruned so that God can remove everything in us that is not Christ-like. And what does this painful process produce in the end?
Beautiful fruit.
The cut is deeper than we think
Some weeks back, a reference was made to the pruning process, and a comment that stayed with me: any horticulturalist will tell you that on a grape vine, 70 to 90 percent of the previous year's growth is cut away for the next season's harvest.
Let that sink in. Not a trim. Not a tidy-up. The vinedresser removes almost everything, leaving only a few bare canes.
Here's why. An unpruned vine still grows, vigorously, in fact. It throws out leaves and shoots in every direction and produces many grapes. But they are small, scattered, sour, and poor. The plant's energy is spread so thin that nothing comes to its full sweetness. The drastic cut does the opposite: it concentrates all the vine's life into a few points, and that is what produces large, rich, concentrated fruit.
This is exactly what Jesus says. "He cuts off every branch in me that bears no fruit, while every branch that does bear fruit he prunes so that it will be even more fruitful" (John 15:2, NIV). Notice, the fruitful branch is the one that gets pruned. Pruning is not God's punishment for failing. It is His investment in a life already bearing. The Greek word translated "prune" also means "to cleanse," and in the very next verse Jesus says, "You are already clean because of the word I have spoken to you" (John 15:3, NIV). The cutting and the cleansing are the same act of love.
So often the things God removes aren't even sins. They're good things that divide our attention and scatter our growth into thin, unremarkable fruit. Surrender means trusting Him to decide what stays.
The season of vulnerability
Here is what struck me most. Pruning happens in a season — in the vine's winter dormancy, when growth has stopped and the plant is at rest. And after the cut, the vine is at its most vulnerable.
Those fresh wounds are open. The tender new growth that pushes out in spring is exposed to frost, wind, and disease before it hardens and gains strength. For a while, the vine doesn't look more fruitful, it looks barer, smaller, more exposed than before.
That is the season the believer fears. After God removes something central, there is a raw, tender window before the new strength comes. We feel diminished, stripped of the things we used to hide behind. And the temptation in that moment is to conclude that God has abandoned us — when in truth, the cut was the clearest evidence of His care for the harvest He sees coming.
Scripture knows this season well: "Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning" (Psalm 30:5, NIV).
And here is the grace of it — the pruned vine is never told to try harder to grow back. It is told one thing: remain. "Remain in me, as I also remain in you. No branch can bear fruit by itself; it must remain in the vine" (John 15:4, NIV). Strength does not return through striving. It returns through staying connected to the Vine.
A word for the one still outside the vineyard
If you don't yet know Christ, this message cuts to you too. The branch that has no living connection to the vine bears nothing at all, however vigorous and green it may look from the outside. The whole picture presses toward a single question. Not "Are you working hard enough?" but "Are you connected to the source of life?"
An invitation to surrender
Complete surrender is letting the Vinedresser hold the shears.
It is trusting that the 70 to 90 percent He cuts away — comforts, plans, securities, even good things — is being removed not to diminish you, but to concentrate His life in you. It is staying rooted through the bare and vulnerable season, believing that what looks like loss is the very making of the harvest.
You will not always understand the cut while it's happening. The branch never does. But the Vinedresser is never careless, never random, and never absent. He knows your vine and your season, your wounds, your capacity and He prunes with the harvest already in view.
So lay down the shears. Stop defending the growth He is reaching for. Remain in Him through the tender season, and trust the One who promised: "This is to my Father's glory, that you bear much fruit, showing yourselves to be my disciples" (John 15:8, NIV).
Surrender, and let Him bring the fruit.

The day Jesus saved my life was a very special day—one that I have reflected on many times over the years. Not long ago, the Holy Spirit brought that moment back to my remembrance once again.

Salvation is a supernatural work of the Holy Spirit. It is the fulfilment of the very purpose for which Jesus sent Him. The Holy Spirit convicts the heart, revealing truth in a way that nothing else can. He penetrates both heart and mind, bringing a clear division between light and darkness, just as the Word of God describes (Hebrews 4:12; John 16:8).

For me, it was a definite and unmistakable revelation of the truth that sets us free (John 8:32). It was the realization that Jesus had paid the full price for sin—once and for all (Hebrews 10:10). In that moment, I understood that salvation was not something I could earn, but a gift of grace purchased through His sacrifice on the cross.

Later in life, however, it became difficult to understand why full victory and a meaningful life sometimes seemed so elusive when they had been promised in Christ (John 10:10). It is only now that I realize there is a process to holiness and a process of discipline that produces fruit in our lives. It is through this process that we begin to experience the fullness of life, purpose, and victory that Jesus intended for us (John 15:5; Hebrews 12:11).

This process involves preparation. It draws us nearer to God and teaches us to hear His voice through the Holy Spirit. It creates a pathway of life, light, and purpose (Psalm 119:105).

So, what is this process?

I believe each of us has our own journey. Our struggles are unique, our life circumstances differ greatly, and the calling God has placed upon each of us is personal and distinct. For me, the process involved God allowing me to make mistakes, because He knew that the end result would always draw me closer to Him due to the posture of my heart.

It required submission to Him in everything.

Nothing hidden.

No shame.

Clean hands.

A pure heart.

"Who may ascend the mountain of the Lord? Who may stand in His holy place? The one who has clean hands and a pure heart" (Psalm 24:3-4).

That surrender is what allowed me to grow in Him.

Tonight, I came to understand more clearly how God draws His people. Our all-knowing Father, who has always known us and had us in His mind long before the foundations of the world were laid (Ephesians 1:4). Read Jeremiah 1 and consider the incredible truth that God knew us before we were born (Jeremiah 1:5).

For me, I had to reach a point of desperation. A place where I was willing to lose everything of earthly value if that was what it took to fully experience His will for my life.

The 23rd of April is a day that will forever remain in my memory.

God knew it would arrive.

I never saw it coming.

It was a life-changing event that caused me to step out of my lifeboat and begin walking on water.

Like Peter stepping out of the boat at Jesus' command (Matthew 14:29), I was called to trust Him beyond my own understanding and beyond the safety of what was familiar.

God loves us infinitely.

But we must ensure that everything we have, everything we do, and everything that surrounds us brings glory to Him.

Everything.

"So whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God" (1 Corinthians 10:31).

My prayer is that you will be encouraged to keep pressing through your own process, no matter how difficult the challenges, trials, or troubles may seem. God uses these seasons to prepare us. He shapes our character, strengthens our faith, and teaches us dependence upon Him.

Do not give up.

The process has a purpose.

One day, you too may find yourself stepping out of the boat and walking on water with Him.

And when that day comes, you will discover that He was preparing you all along.

Thank You, Jesus, for the indescribable gift You gave us through Your sacrifice, Your grace, and Your unfailing love.

To God be all the glory.

title.$t: A special message: ALL IS NOT LOST

content.$t:
Good evening. Wow.. I never thought I would post again so soon, but God spoke to me.                                        So here goes:              Tonight I watched a YouTube video of country star Eric Church delivering a commencement speech at Kenan Stadium, the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, on May 9, 2026. The speech has been going viral, and for good reason. It was surprisingly powerful, centered on faith, family, marriage, ambition, community, and personal growth. Using the six strings of a guitar as a metaphor for life’s six pillars, Church gave the graduates a message many say is missing from college campuses today.
As I listened, I found myself reflecting back to when I was that age. In the 1980s, we didn’t have messages like this. I wondered what my life would have been like if I had received that kind of inspiration and influence. My parents divorced when I was 12, my brother was 9, and my sister was not even a year old. For us, it was always about survival. For me, inspiration had to come from within, because there was nobody cheering me on from the sidelines. The message was clear: make it. If you do, great. If you don’t, you haven’t measured up to the world’s standards, whatever that meant at the time.
My father could never fully be the strict “bad dad” after the divorce, although he had been very strict when he lived with us. Seeing us only two nights out of every fourteen meant those visits always had to be “good.” I am now 55, and at this time in my life I have been reflecting on all of this more deeply. Tonight, as I listened to the speech, the Holy Spirit spoke to me.
Even though you may think you have missed out on great opportunities and life events because no one cheered you on or inspired you to be greater, there is one thing you can never forget: Your greatest cheerleader in life is God Himself!
Scripture says, “Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, before you were born I set you apart; I appointed you as a prophet to the nations” (Jeremiah 1:5, NIV). This tells us that God thought about us before conception. Another scripture says, “He chose us in Him before the creation of the world” (Ephesians 1:4). Imagine that! God was thinking of us, alive here in 2026, even before 4004 BC.
The Holy Spirit also said to me that the God we serve will take everything we thought was lost, forgotten, or missed, and restore it to us three times, five times, even seven times more in the days we have left. But this will only be for those who know Him. You see, when you have had an encounter with the living God through the power of the Holy Spirit, nothing makes sense except who you are in Him.
Tonight, someone needs to hear this. There are people out there living in the disappointments of their past, and all they really need is to meet Jesus. That’s all. In that moment, purpose, destiny, and the meaning of life will finally make sense for the first time. I want to encourage you to share this message far and wide. The devil has convinced so many people that they missed the best of their lives, and he has given them every justification to believe it. He is the father of lies. God will restore and bring back more into your life than you could ever imagine. God is your biggest cheerleader!

Good evening.

This is a personal story.
Not so long ago, without me knowing or being aware of it, I was getting up every day in a bit of a comfort zone. Just a little bit. Then one email changed everything. On 4 June 2024, my contract was terminated. I had poured my heart and soul into that company for five years.
I was devastated. I didn’t know how to handle it. Very quickly I realised I was in trouble. There was no income in the foreseeable future. There were no prospects. Anxiety set in. I prayed with my heart in my mouth. A huge amount of emotions flooded my soul.
Our son was in matric. Life came to a standstill. I will never forget the moment I had to tell my wife that I lost my job. I felt rejected, alone, and helpless. But somehow, only by God’s grace, we made it. For the next four months we lived in that grace. Then a breakthrough came. A contract job that sustained our family for 18 months. It lasted till 23 April 2026.
Before I tell you what happened next, it is important for context. From June 2025 till December 2025 I was on a spiritual journey that turned my life around completely. I carry a very deep personal testimony of how God can enter your life and heal you. This healing reached many years of disappointments and pain, some going back 43 years.
At the start of 2026 we decided to minister to people. We wanted to share what God has been doing in our lives. So we started a life group in February 2026. Since then we have seen our lives become wrapped in the Holy Spirit’s guidance and God’s Word.
23 April 2026 came the same as 4 June 2024. But this time it was different. Although I was devastated and emotional, an inner peace started to push through. The voice of God broke through the moments of disappointment  And I was struggeling with a big question?
Why am I here again?
In the middle of the fire?
In both storms, certain portions of Scripture became my anchor. They were not just verses I read. They were the words that kept me breathing.
Matthew 6 became my daily bread. Jesus said do not worry about your life. He spoke of what we will eat or drink, about our body and what we will wear. Those words confronted my anxiety. I read them slowly each morning. If the Father feeds the birds and clothes the lilies, He sees me too. Seek first His kingdom.
John chapters 15, 16 and 17 carried me deeper. John 15 taught me to abide in the Vine. John 16 told me trouble would come, but to take heart because He has overcome the world. John 17 is Jesus’ prayer for His disciples. Knowing He prayed for me brought me to tears and gave me great comfort.
Ephesians chapters 1, 2 and 3 restored my identity. I am chosen, adopted, redeemed and sealed. I am saved by grace, not by my performance or contracts. His love has height, depth, length and width. God is able to do immeasurably more than all I can ask or imagine.
These passages did not remove the pain instantly. But they reshaped my heart inside the fire. My life is not defined by a company’s decision. It rests in the unchanging Word of a faithful God.
If you are walking through loss or disappointment right now, sit with these chapters. Read them slowly. Let them speak louder than your fears. They can sustain you too.
I still don’t have all the answers. But this season feels different. The fear has lost its full power. Something deeper has taken root.
I will share more as the story unfolds. You are not alone.
Stay encouraged.
Carl

Good morning, 

The last couple of weeks were a very busy time. Apologies for the break, but I am back, and today I share something that I believe is the most important part of a Christian's life on this earth. Acknowledging the Holy Spirit daily at all times in every moment. 

Background:

The Farewell Discourse in John 13–17, also called the Upper Room Discourse, contains Jesus’ final private teachings to his disciples following the Last Supper. In these chapters, Jesus washes their feet, commands them to love one another as he has loved them, promises the Holy Spirit, and uses the vine-and-branches image to stress that we must abide in him.

Content:

There is a moment in the Gospel of John where Jesus says something that must have unsettled His disciples. In John 15, He speaks of leaving them, of a coming separation they were not ready to face. But yet in the same breath, He gives a promise that carries more weight than their fear. Jesus spoke of the Advocate.

In John 15:26 (NIV), Jesus says, “When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who goes out from the Father, he will testify about me.” The word translated “Advocate” comes from the Greek paraklētos (παράκλητος). It is a rich word. It means one who is called alongside, a helper in the closest sense, one who stands with you, not at a distance but right beside you in the moment of need. It can also carry the sense of a legal defender, someone who speaks on your behalf when you cannot.

In John 16, the meaning deepens. Jesus says, “It is for your good that I am going away. Unless I go away, the Advocate will not come to you; but if I go, I will send him to you” (John 16:7, NIV). For the disciples, this must have sounded impossible. How could anything be better than having Jesus physically present with them? Yet Jesus was revealing something they could not yet grasp. His departure would make way for a presence no longer limited to one place.

The Spirit is described as the “Spirit of truth.” The Greek word for truth here is alētheia (ἀλήθεια), which carries the sense of what is uncovered, what is no longer hidden. Truth, in this sense, is not just correct information. It is reality as God sees it, fully revealed. When Jesus says the Spirit will testify, the verb behind this idea carries the meaning of bearing witness, like someone who speaks from direct knowledge. The Spirit does not speculate. He reveals what is real.

Jesus explains that the Advocate will convict the world concerning sin, righteousness, and judgment (John 16:8). The word “convict” comes from the Greek elenchō (ἐλέγχω). It does not mean to shame or condemn harshly. It means to expose, to bring something into the light so it can be seen clearly. There is a purpose in this. What is hidden cannot be healed. The Spirit reveals not to destroy, but to restore.

He goes further and says, “But when he, the Spirit of truth, comes, he will guide you into all the truth” (John 16:13, NIV). The word “guide” comes from hodēgeō (ὁδηγέω), which paints the picture of someone leading the way on a journey. Not pushing from behind, but walking ahead, showing the path step by step. This is not a forced direction. It is relational guidance, the kind that requires trust and attentiveness. Understand this is a big and important truth for us as believers to search for that direction. 

Why did Jesus send the Holy Spirit? Because His mission was never meant to remain external. While He walked the earth, people could follow Him physically. But through the Spirit, that following becomes internal. The presence of God moves from beside us to within us. The Advocate is not simply near. He dwells in the very center of our lives.

For everyday life, this changes everything. The Spirit becomes the quiet voice that steadies decisions, the inner conviction that redirects when we begin to drift, the reassurance that settles fear when circumstances feel uncertain. There is a nearness that cannot be replicated by anything else. Not dramatic or overwhelming most of the time, but steady and faithful.

There is also a deeper purpose in how the Spirit works. Jesus says, “He will glorify me because it is from me that he will receive what he will make known to you” (John 16:14, NIV). The word “glorify” comes from the Greek doxazō (δοξάζω), which means to reveal the true nature or worth of something. The Spirit’s role is not to draw attention to Himself, but to make Jesus fully known. To bring clarity to who He is, not just in thought, but in lived experience.

So the promise of the Advocate is not distant or abstract. It is deeply personal. The One who is called alongside us is also the One who lives within us. The One who reveals truth is also the One who gently leads us into it.

What the disciples first heard as loss became something far greater. The presence they once saw with their eyes became a presence they would carry within them every day.

It is the prayer of my heart that you will become intensely aware of the Holy Spirit right now. Right next to you. Advocating on your behalf in all you trust God for in this life. He will support you, guide you, heal you, and deliver you.  

May you have amazing experiences with the Holy Spirit for the rest of your life!!   

God bless you.

Carl.

title.$t: Crucifixion to Resurrection: The Compelling Evidence from the Shroud of Turin

content.$t:
Good afternoon!

This weekend has really been one of those quiet, meaningful times for me. As God’s children, we’re supposed to pause and think about what the big Christian holidays actually stand for, and Easter is right at the top of that list.

I’ve spent most of the week just sitting with the deeper side of Jesus’ death and what it really means for me personally. It really hit different this year. And I know it's because I have been searching Him more than ever before.

Then this morning at church… wow. Watching people step forward and give their lives to Christ was the highlight of the whole weekend. It felt like the Holy Spirit was right there in the room with us. Such a powerful time.

You know how it goes every year, churches share a ton of messages around Easter. And honestly, a lot of people who don’t normally come only show up for funerals, weddings, or Easter services.

We saw that this weekend with the packed seats from the Auditorium to the overflow cube, and the entrance and passage way had seats packed.

I want to share a couple of simple, really valuable truths from this weekend and the next 40 days ahead. I think they’ll bless you.

I am about to share a lot of facts from studies and data I read and watched this week. And I would like to share it with you.

Credit: Dr Jeremiah Johnson

Crucifixion Details (From the Shroud of Turin and Supporting Artifacts)

The Shroud of Turin carries real human bloodstains of type AB.

These stains match the wounds you would expect on a first-century Roman crucifixion victim, and they line up exactly with the blood on the Sudarium of Oviedo—the separate face cloth mentioned in the Gospel of John.

 

Facts About the Shroud of Turin (Age, Dimensions, Blood Stains)

Importantly, the bloodstains were already on the cloth before the body image ever appeared. There is no image underneath any of the blood, which shows the body was wrapped soon after death,h and the image formed later.

A Roman flagrum (a type of scourge) with lead balls and dumbbells attached to rawhide thongs delivered around 372 lashes or more. That level of beating caused roughly one-third of the victim’s total blood loss, including strikes to the pelvic area and possible damage around the eyes.


A crown of thorns replica showed puncture wounds that match the head injuries visible on the Shroud.

 

The real crown of thorns looks like this

The crucifixion nails were square-shaft iron from the first century—some bent from being reused—and driven through the wrists and feet. Archaeologists have even found a heel bone in Jerusalem pierced by a nail of the same type, confirming how the Romans carried out these executions.

Soldiers gambled for the victim’s clothing using dice, just as the Gospels describe.

Roman Dice

Thirty Tyrian silver pieces represent the exact amount of the temple tax that was paid to Judas for the betrayal.

Finally, pollen grains trapped in the Shroud come only from plants that grow in the Jerusalem area, which places the cloth’s origin right there in the right time and place.

Resurrection Evidence (The Shroud of Turin as a Physical “Receipt”)

The image on the Shroud is incredibly thin—only 0.02 microns thick—and it affects just the very top fibers of the linen. There are no pigments, dyes, or paint anywhere on it, ruling out any kind of medieval forgery or artistic creation.

 Shroud Images

In 1976, NASA’s VP-8 image analyzer revealed that the image contained three-dimensional holographic data. That property simply does not show up in normal paintings or photographs.

 VP-8 Image Analyzer and Set-up Research 3D Materials

The full-body image formed in a split second with an enormous burst of energy—estimated at 34,000 billion watts, something like a nuclear event—dated to April 5, AD 33. Jesus’ body “emanated through” the cloth, leaving no decay fluids behind.

When photographer Secondo Pia developed his glass-plate photos of the Shroud in 1898, the image suddenly appeared as a photographic negative for the first time.

How did the Turin Shroud get its image?

There are no signs of body decomposition on the cloth, which fits with the body being taken out after only a short time, hours, not days.

The 1988 carbon-dating test that suggested a medieval date has been discredited. The sample came from a patched corner that mixed cotton and linen, not the original cloth, and the raw data were kept secret for 27 years by the British Museum. Later studies now support a first-century origin.

More recently, both the image and the bloodstains have started to fade because of light and oxygen exposure. Today, the Shroud is kept in a special reliquary filled with 99 percent argon gas to protect it.

Byzantine coins from the late seventh century, such as the Justinian Solidus, show a face with more than 200 exact matching points to the Shroud image. These are the earliest known portraits of Jesus on currency, appearing right around the time of the Islamic conquests.

Byzantine Coins, the Shroud of Turin, and the Holy Grail – The Coins & History Foundation

The Shroud is described as an “itemized receipt of love,” pointing to Romans 5:8 (NIV). It stands as physical proof that the same body that was crucified and buried later left the cloth in a supernatural way.

Key Historical and Textual Facts That Support the Crucifixion and Resurrection

We have more than 5,800 New Testament manuscripts and fragments today. Among the earliest are Papyrus 52 (around 125 AD, containing John 20:31-38) and Papyrus 64 (the oldest known piece of Matthew). There are 45 independent historical sources for Jesus within the first hundred years after His death—more evidence than we have for many well-accepted ancient events, like the Battle of Franklin in the Civil War.

The Great Isaiah Scroll, found at Qumran and written about 250 years before Jesus, is remarkably stable. Its text matches manuscripts written a thousand years later, including the famous suffering-servant passage in Isaiah 53 that Christians connect directly to the crucifixion.

                                                       The Great Isaiah Scroll

Codex Vaticanus, from around 330–325 AD, is the earliest nearly complete Greek Bible. When you compare it to modern translations, the wording holds steady across the centuries.

The James ossuary, inscribed “James, son of Joseph, brother of Jesus,” fits the historical picture perfectly. James started out as a sceptic of Jesus (see Mark 3 and John 7:5 NIV). After he saw the risen Jesus (1 Corinthians 15:7 NIV), he became a believer, led the early church, and was martyred around AD 62—something the historian Josephus also records.

The James Ossuary

Roman coins served as the official “social media” of the day. Inscriptions like “Tiberius, son of Augustus, son of God, Pontifex Maximus” stand in sharp contrast to Jesus’ own claims to be the true Son of God and High Priest.

A replica of a Roman needle helps explain the “eye of the needle” metaphor in Mark 10:25 (NIV). It drives home that earning salvation by human effort is impossible—Jesus paid the full debt on the cross.

Two hostile witnesses completely changed their lives after claiming to see the risen Jesus: James (Jesus’ own brother) and Paul (who had been a persecutor of Christians). Both became key leaders in the church.

First-century Jewish culture worked against inventing a resurrection story. Jews believed in one general resurrection at the end of time, not an individual rising in the middle of history. The claim was culturally embarrassing and therefore unlikely to be made up.

The evidence is summarized with eight solid reasons that together make the case for the resurrection:

1.     It gives a meaningful framework for understanding suffering (Romans 8:18 NIV).

2.     Jesus predicted it multiple times.

3.     He publicly demonstrated power over death in miracles, including raising Lazarus.

4.     The Gospels themselves are strongly supported by textual and archaeological evidence.

5.     There was no cultural or psychological reason for first-century Jews to invent the story.

6.     Hostile witnesses like James and Paul were converted.

7.     The Gospel message brought radical social freedom and rehumanized society.

8.     The Shroud of Turin itself stands as powerful physical evidence.

These points come straight from careful examination of the artifacts and records. They show that the crucifixion and resurrection are backed by more than just ancient texts—they’re supported by physical objects, scientific study, and historical context that still hold up today.

 I trust this has been of great value to you!

My next blog, "The Advocate," is an awesome revelation the Holy Spirit is sharing with me!

link.title: Crucifixion to Resurrection: The Compelling Evidence from the Shroud of Turin

"Return of the Prodigal Son" by Rembrandt (c. 1668–1669) depicts a powerful scene of forgiveness. The kneeling son, dressed in tattered clothes, presses into his father’s chest in repentance. The father, in a warm, flowing robe, gently places his hands on the son’s back, symbolizing love and acceptance.

Good afternoon

As I was praying last night, this topic gently jumped into my heart. How many of us can testify that we see and experience God’s love for us every single day?

As we journey through life, it’s natural to think that God is far away—looking down on us mere mortals from a vast distance, residing in the third heaven. But that simply isn’t true. There is so much scripture we can reference that shows us the opposite.

Psalm 139:7-10 (NIV) “Where can I go from your Spirit? Where can I flee from your presence? If I go up to the heavens, you are there; if I make my bed in the depths, you are there. If I rise on the wings of the dawn, if I settle on the far side of the sea, even there your hand will guide me, your right hand will hold me fast.”

What a beautiful scripture, making it clear that God is always close to us, everywhere on earth. He is ever present.

Another scripture that speaks to this is:

John 14:16-17 (NIV) “And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever— the Spirit of truth. The world cannot accept him, because it neither sees him nor knows him. But you know him, for he lives with you and will be in you.”

Jesus promises the Holy Spirit as a permanent Helper who dwells with and in believers. This shows God’s active presence on earth through the Spirit—not as a distant force, but as an indwelling reality for those who follow Christ.

The question I started with is this: Can you see God’s love every day?

For those of us who are privileged to have children, we know the depth of emotion and the many actions we pour out toward them. Here is a list:

Emotions Love Compassion Joy / Delight Concern / Worry Tenderness Protectiveness Pride Hope Patience Gratitude / Thankfulness Forgiveness Empathy Awe / Wonder

Actions Providing comfort Ensuring safety Offering protection Providing provision Nurturing Showing affection Disciplining / Training Teaching and instructing Encouraging and affirming Listening and communicating Sacrificing Spending quality time Forgiving and showing mercy Guiding and directing Respecting and honoring Celebrating Supporting emotionally Mentoring

All of the above flows from the source of love.

Imagine what Father God’s heart posture is toward us when such a standard is our reference for how we love our own children. In a loving home, all the children will experience these attributes from good parents. It’s often only when they grow more mature and more wise that they come to truly recognise what we as parents do for them.

So if we sit still and think about the evidence of God’s love in our lives and it’s not so clear, could it be that we simply need to grow a little more in Him? To spend more time with Him?

Look at this:

Romans 8:28 (NIV) “And we know that in all things God works for the good of those who love him and have been called according to his purpose.”

What This Means

This verse assures us that God’s love is actively present and working even in the hardest, most confusing, or painful situations of life, not just the good ones. Nothing is wasted. Because of His great love for us, He weaves all things together for our ultimate benefit and according to His perfect purpose.

It also ties in beautifully with the parental love I mentioned earlier: just as a loving parent turns every effort (comfort, protection, provision, nurturing, etc.) toward their child’s best interest out of love, God does the same for us—only perfectly and in all things.

So I want to encourage you today: seek Him and be on the lookout for God��s love in your life.

He is all around you, every second of every day.

God bless you!!

title.$t: The Holy Spirit Is Waiting for you

Good afternoon,

In the beginning, God created heaven and earth. And the earth was without form and void, and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters. And God said, "Let there be light," and there was light. (Genesis 1:1-3 KJV)

We’ve all read these opening verses of the Bible countless times.

We picture the nothingness, the formless void, the thick darkness. But then God speaks, and in a moment, light explodes into existence. But there was something truly special that happened in that moment that I never stopped to notice: the Holy Spirit was already there, waiting.

Before a single word left God’s mouth, verse 2 tells us the Spirit of God was moving—hovering, brooding—over the face of the waters.

The Hebrew word “moved” (rachaph) paints a picture of a mother bird gently fluttering over her nest, expectant and ready. The Spirit wasn’t passive; the Holy Spirit was positioned perfectly, waiting for the creative Word from God the Father to be released so He could perform it.

Think about that sequence. The Trinity in perfect harmony: the Father had the plan, the Word was spoken, and the Holy Spirit executed the instruction. The moment God declared, “Let there be light,” the Spirit sprang into action and brought order out of chaos. I have never before thought about the creation process taking place in this way.

And the most amazing part? This wasn't just ancient history. It’s the exact pattern God designed for our life today.

If you are a believer, the same Holy Spirit who hovered over those primeval waters now lives inside us. (1 Corinthians 6:19). He’s not distant or inactive—He’s hovering right now over all the “formless and void” areas of our life: maybe a broken marriage, an empty bank account, a sick body, or a hopeless situation. He’s waiting… just like in Genesis.

He’s waiting for us to do what God did: speak the Word.

We need to pray bold declarations! Scripture is clear—death and life are in the power of the tongue (Proverbs 18:21). Jesus commanded us to speak to mountains, and they would obey (Mark 11:23). Why? Because when we release God’s written Word from our lips in faith, the Holy Spirit moves immediately to perform it, just as He did at creation.

Start speaking today. Over your health: “By His stripes I am healed” (Isaiah 53:5). Over your finances: “My God shall supply all my need” (Philippians 4:19). Over fear: “God has not given me a spirit of fear” (2 Timothy 1:7). Say it out loud. Declare it with authority. The Holy Spirit is listening, ready to turn your darkness into light.

This revelation has changed my way of thinking and the way I will approach my prayer life. I will now stop waiting on God to move and start moving the hand of God by faith by speaking His Word. The results I will be trusting for will be breakthrough after breakthrough.

Friend, the Spirit is hovering over your situation right now. He’s waiting for your voice. Open your mouth and release the Word. Let there be light in your life—because when the Word goes forth, the Holy Spirit always performs it.

We need to speak it today.

link.title: The Holy Spirit Is Waiting for you

title.$t: God Can Redeem Your Wasted Years

content.$t:
As I was driving this week and listening to a teaching, as I often do, this one was sent to me by a friend. And after listening to it, I was inspired to share a message that is

VERY INSPIRING FOR OUR FUTURES!

Many of us only got saved, not at a younger age but at 30, 40, or 50 years old. And as you build a relationship with God over the years, you start asking some questions.

Do you ever look at your life and think, “I should be further along by now”? Maybe you feel behind in your career, or your spiritual growth, your calling, or even your understanding of who you really are.

If that thought has ever crossed your mind, you're not alone — and the important thing is, you're not in trouble.

In this blog I want us to open Jeremiah 1, because it delivers one of the most freeing truths I've ever heard:

“How many of us feel, hands on heart, ‘I am behind the time of my own development. I should be further on than I am right now.’”

There is a profound truth that I want to share:

Did you know that we serve the God of the universe who can redeem time? Did you know that He can speed up your development? Are you aware that God can get you back on track no matter how much time you have wasted or feel you have wasted in your life? He can redeem time. (I had to wrap my head around that, to be honest.)

This single truth has changed how I see my entire journey with God.

FACT: Your life story started before you were born

Here is something breathtaking in Jeremiah 1:5:

“Before I formed you in the womb I knew you. Before you were born I consecrated you. I have appointed you…”

Your existence in God's heart preceded your conception.

This is a truth that has penetrated my heart very deeply, as I now have a different understanding of God's greatness, almightiness, power, and holiness.

FACT: Your identity is not based on who you came through but who you came from.

God does not look at your paternity, your father or mother (who you came through). God knows where you come from — from HIM!

FACT: Your purpose didn't begin the day you decided to follow Jesus. It began in the heart of God, before you took your first breath.

Isn't that amazing? I have come to the realisation that the purpose in my life has only one source: God. No matter where I try and search for my purpose in life, I can only find it in Him.

When was the last time you felt “behind”? What if that feeling is actually an opportunity or an invitation to let God step into your life and redeem your life's timeline?

God Is Not Bothered by Who You Are Not

Let's look at Jeremiah.

Jeremiah's response to God's instruction to him was, “Alas, Lord God… I don’t know how to speak because I’m a youth.”

God's reply? “Do not say, ‘I am a youth.’ … Do not be afraid… for I am with you to deliver you.”

LESSON: The Lord has never really been all that bothered about who you are not. In my experience of Him, He is overjoyed at what He can make you into.

If we break up our lives into responsibility quadrants on a pie chart, guaranteed that God wants the lion’s share of the responsibility for your life.

We are His partner, but God is always the bigger one.

The Two Relationships we as believers have with God

This truth hits hard:

We always have at least two relationships with God:

  1. As much-loved children, we come to Him simply and freely, and we are accepted as we are.
  2. As a developing, fully mature son/daughter (stepping into responsibility and destiny)

When we approach God in prayer and when we have conversation with Him, we should always come to God devotionally from the place of a much-loved child…

God makes everything so simple so that we can step into it.

Then we grow from there.

Practical Steps to Catch Up in our life Development

  • Come to God as a loved child every day (with no performance, with no striving)
  • Ask the right questions: “What does this mean, Father God? And what do I need to do?”
  • Believe that God is speeding up your development right now
  • Let your purpose open the pathway to your true identity, calling, and destiny

I want to end by saying:

  • You are not late.
  • You are not behind.
  • You are exactly where the God who knew you before you were born wants you to be. Allow Him to accelerate you from here.

Final word: “None of us need to be worried about it. We just need to take our slippers off and put some running shoes on… because we’ve got some ground to make up.”

God bless and lots of love

Carl.

Good Evening,

There's a secret worth sharing—one that happens every single day, yet so few people truly notice it or let it sink in. After you read this, I hope you'll pass it on, wherever life takes you—high and low, to friends, family, strangers. It could change someone's day.

In this huge world of ours, I talk to people all the time who tell me how alone they feel. Honestly, I've been there too. When life hit hard and things fell apart, I pulled away and isolated myself. But not everyone ends up alone by choice—sometimes circumstances, pain, or shame just push people there.

Think back to Genesis 3:8–9. Right after the fall, something brand new happens in human history. Adam and Eve hide from God, suddenly aware of their nakedness and the weight of their sin. And God calls out the very first question recorded in Scripture: "Where are you?"

That wasn't God lost or needing directions. He knew exactly where they were. It was a tender, searching call to come back into relationship. From that moment, through more than 4,000 years of Old Testament story—from Abraham to the prophets—God has been the One pursuing us, chasing after His lost children.

It all built to that perfect moment in Galatians 4:4: "When the fullness of time had come, God sent forth His Son." God sent His Son to find His bride, because we were lost—like the one sheep that wandered off. He couldn't leave us that way.

Being lost carries heavy consequences. Without knowing our secure place in Jesus, life feels like drifting on an endless ocean with no rudder. Our sinful nature pulls us away, and the results can be devastating. Just look at what Adam and Eve faced right away:

  • Immediate shame and the awareness of nakedness (Genesis 3:7)
  • Fear that drove them to hide (Genesis 3:8–10)
  • Blame-shifting and excuses (Genesis 3:11–13)
  • Curses bringing hard labor, painful childbirth, and thorns (Genesis 3:14–19)
  • Being driven out of Eden, losing paradise (Genesis 3:22–24)
  • Death entering the world (Genesis 3:19; Romans 5:12)
  • Broken relationships and family heartbreak (Genesis 3:16; 4:1–16)
  • Separation from God's close presence (Genesis 3:23–24)

Satan loves to twist the truth about who we really are in Christ. He whispers shame, self-rejection, and this false idea that we're failures in God's eyes. Those lies create distance, isolation, a chasm. So many today hide—because of old sins, shattered relationships, unspoken regrets—and they carry this invisible measuring stick of "not good enough." It's like living half-asleep in a nightmare, going through the motions, even showing up at church, but never really stepping into God's presence.

But here's the beautiful, unshakable truth: God never stops searching.

His whole redemptive story—from the Garden to the Cross—was one long, determined pursuit to bring us back. No matter how long we've ignored Him, turned away, or hidden—the answer to "Is God still looking for me?" is a loud, loving YES!

And there's this hidden treasure tucked right in the Hebrew of Scripture that shows just how personal and daily that pursuit is.

Read it with me in the King James Version—Job 7:17–18:

What is man, that thou shouldest magnify him? and that thou shouldest set thine heart upon him? And that thou shouldest visit him every morning, and try him every moment?

These words echo Psalm 8:4 ("What is man that You are mindful of him?"), but Job says them from a place of raw pain.

In Hebrew, the word translated "visit" is pāqad (פָּקַד). This isn't a casual drop-by. It's purposeful—God paying close, intentional attention. Think of how God "visited" Sarah and she bore Isaac (Genesis 21), or how He "visited" Israel to deliver them from Egypt (Exodus 3–4), or "visited" Hannah so Samuel was born. Pāqad means God steps in with care, intervention, even deliverance.

And "morning"? That's bōqer (בֹּקֶר)—literally dawn, the break of day. When the text says "every morning," it means every single morning—day after day, as sure as the sun rises, without fail.

Paired with "every moment," it shows God's attention is relentless: He meets us fresh at each new dawn and stays close every instant.

Job wasn't describing a distant God here. He felt overwhelmed by One who seemed too close—turning toward him every single sunrise. In his suffering, it felt like constant scrutiny. But flip the perspective, and what a revelation: God visits every day.

This ties straight to Lamentations 3:22–23: "His mercies are new every morning." Before your eyes even open, God has already pāqad you—right there in your bedroom, your hospital room, your broken place. Across more than 8.7 billion lives, every single day, through His Holy Spirit.

So here's the message of hope:

You are never alone. Not ever. Every sunrise is God's quiet, steady reminder: "I'm here—right now—visiting you with My presence, My mercy, My power."

Maybe shift your first thought from "Good morning, Lord" to recognizing He's already been pursuing you through the night. Stop hiding. Step out. Let Him find you fully.

In a world full of shame and defeat, hear this: God visits every morning—that's you, me, the person sitting right next to you. Hallelujah!

title.$t: Allowing good seed in our life

content.$t:
Good morning,

The last week we have had a tough, difficult week. We can all associate with those types of weeks. Both Wilma and I had a serious bout of flu that we needed to navigate.

I want to share an interesting subject that the Holy Spirit spoke into my heart. I heard very clearly these words spoken into my spirit: "corruptible" and "incorruptible seed," and what followed was an amazing experience. 

Not only was the sermon on Sunday morning exactly on that topic matter, but it also made me sit and spend time on what this really means.

1. How the Rebirth (Being Born Again) Takes Place Imagine you’re planting a tiny seed in your garden. The old, natural way we’re born is like planting in poor, rocky soil—it’s the “perishable seed” we all start with. It grows for a while, but eventually it withers because of hurts, mistakes, and the brokenness sin brings into every life.

But God offers something far better. 1 Peter 1:23 (NIV) says: “For you have been born again, not of perishable seed, but of imperishable, through the living and enduring word of God.”

Practically, the rebirth happens like this:

  • Someone (or you reading the Bible) simply shares the good news: Jesus loves you so much He died on the cross to take away every sin and rose again so you can have eternal life with Him.
  • In that moment, you open your heart and say something honest and simple like, “Jesus, I believe You died for me. I’m sorry for my wrongs. Come into my life and make me new.”
  • That’s it! The Holy Spirit plants the imperishable seed, the living Word, right into your heart. You don’t have to clean yourself up first. God does the miracle. You are born again instantly, just like a baby taking its first breath. For me it was the realisation that over a period of a week after I invited Christ into my life, that my mannerisms, and the way I spoke, and the way I used to react has changed. 


2. How Our Heart Actually Changes Right at that moment, God keeps a wonderful promise from the Old Testament:

Ezekiel 36:26-27 (NIV) “I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit in you; I will remove from you your heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh. And I will put my Spirit in you and move you to follow my decrees and be careful to keep my laws.”

Your old heart—maybe hardened by pain, anger, shame, or just feeling far from God. It then becomes soft and alive. And suddenly you notice:

  • You want to talk to God like a friend.
  • Sin doesn’t feel as appealing.
  • You start caring about people the way Jesus does.

It’s not that you have become perfect overnight (none of us do!), but the direction of your heart flips. The Holy Spirit moves in and begins changing desires from the inside out. You’ll catch yourself thinking, “I used to react with anger, but now I feel peace instead.” That’s the new heart at work!

3. This is an ongoing process, but we have to ALLOW it.

The Holy Spirit is like the gentle gardener who keeps tending your heart-garden. He wants to bring healing to every hurt and help you forgive so bitterness doesn’t choke the beautiful new life. And many other things are impacted as well.

So by applying certain principles like,

  • Opening the Bible daily (even 5-10 minutes).
  • Talking to Him all day 
  • Choosing forgiveness as an act of trust in faith
  • Letting the fruit grow. As you keep saying “yes” to the Spirit, you’ll see His beautiful fruit appearing: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control (Galatians 5:22-23 NIV). These are signs of healing—especially gentleness when you forgive and kindness when you’ve been wounded.
  • Staying close to other believers. Like plants growing together in a garden, we encourage one another and remind each other of God’s promises.
Making the right life choices and applying some principles, we allow the Holy Spirit to step in and sow seeds of love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, and self-control. 

And the fruit of this is the change we experience in ourselves and in our lives.

Allow the Holy Spirit to sow incorruptible seed in your life everyday.

God bless you!
